data.title: Beam Global targets positive cash flow around $11.5M quarterly revenue while expanding BeamHeat push
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Beam Global (BEEM) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Revenue in the third quarter was $6.7 million. It's up 15% year-over-year, and our gross margin improved to 21.3% or 31.9% on an adjusted non-GAAP basis from roughly breakeven in the third quarter of last year." (Chief Financial Officer Lisa Potok)

  • "Commercial customers represented 92% of revenue in the quarter and 56% of our sales came from outside the United States." (CFO Potok)

  • "Backlog ended September at $6.9 million. It's up 28% from the end of June, and our cash balance is up 67% since the start of the year." (CFO Potok)

  • "We also completed the relocation of our manufacturing operations to Yuma, Arizona, a move we expect to generate approximately $3 million in rent savings over the 5-year lease term." (CFO Potok)

  • "Some of you may have seen that we announced earlier this week the introduction of a new product. It's called BeamHeat." (Chairman, CEO, President & Secretary Desmond Wheatley) "It provides 10 hours of heat, cooking, light and recharging a portable devices." (CEO Wheatley)

  • "We experienced a precipitous drop in our share price" during the ScoutDI acquisition process, and "it would not have been right to close on an acquisition" in that market backdrop. (CEO Wheatley)

Outlook

  • "We expect margins to continue to improve as our volume grows" and as "our cost reduction initiatives, including the move to Yuma takes further effect." (CFO Potok)

  • "At around $11.5 million in revenue, we could generate positive cash flow." (CEO Wheatley) "We get to $15 million a quarter... [and] produce... around $1 million a quarter." (CEO Wheatley) "At $22 million in revenue... then we will produce net income and cash flow of over $3 million in a quarter." (CEO Wheatley)

  • "With the strongest El Niño ever approaching the West Coast, we may find needs and hence opportunities for it closer to home, and we certainly do intend to market it globally." (CEO Wheatley)

Financial Results

  • "Our third quarter revenue was $6.7 million" versus "$5.8 million in the third quarter of 2025." (CFO Potok)

  • "We reported $1.4 million or a gross margin of 21.3%" versus "a gross loss of $28,000 or a negative 0.5%" a year earlier; "our adjusted non-GAAP gross margin was 31.9%" versus "12.8%". (CFO Potok)

  • "As for our operating expenses, they came in at $5.9 million compared to $4.8 million a year ago" with the increase "primarily related" to higher "noncash stock-based compensation," "legal expenses" and "costs associated with the relocation of our facilities." (CFO Potok)

  • "Our net loss was $4.5 million compared to $4.9 million" a year earlier; "excluding" noncash items, "our non-GAAP net loss was $2.5 million... $0.11 per share" versus "$0.16 per share". (CFO Potok)

  • "We ended the quarter with $1.6 million in cash" and "remain debt-free with an unused $100 million line of credit." (CFO Potok)

Q&A

  • Andrew (for Craig Irwin), ROTH Capital Partners: asked about gross margin trajectory as the company scales; Chief Executive Officer Wheatley said "we're clearly on that path... to that 50% gross margin," adding "the simple thing that solves for this is just more volume" and pointing to Yuma enabling more vertical integration such as bringing coatings in-house.

  • Andrew (for Craig Irwin), ROTH Capital Partners: asked what is driving European growth; CEO Wheatley replied "across the board" and said newer products are entering "tenders now," while also emphasizing legacy infrastructure and potential Ukraine rebuilding demand.

  • Tate Sullivan, Maxim Group: asked how long BeamHeat had been in development; CEO Wheatley said "it's been a quick development process" and added "if I had a container load of them sitting here right now, they'd all be gone by tomorrow morning."

  • Tate Sullivan, Maxim Group: asked about inventory strategy; CEO Wheatley said "for products like BeamHeat... we're going to want to maintain a lot of inventory" but reiterated "I'd like to run a 0 backlog business" and described "rightsizing" inventory to respond quickly without tying up capital.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly positive and detail-oriented, with margin durability and European growth as repeat themes, framed as requests for "color" on what is "working well" and how growth is "coming from" different product lines.

  • Management tone in prepared remarks was positive and assertive, using confidence language such as "I'm confident" and repeatedly tying strategy to diversification and margin improvement, while also acknowledging stock pressure with phrases like "the share price is shocking to me." (CEO Wheatley)

  • Versus Q2, management commentary shifted from reacceleration off a weak Q1 to highlighting product launches (BeamHeat), Ukraine-related demand exploration, and explicit cash-flow math around quarterly revenue thresholds.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 emphasized diversification outcomes in mix and geography, with CFO Potok stating "Commercial customers represented 92% of revenue" and "56%... from outside the United States," while Q2 emphasized a sharp sequential rebound and backlog conversion.

  • Q3 introduced BeamHeat and highlighted terminated M&A, with CEO Wheatley discussing the "terminated acquisition of ScoutDI" and the stock-price impact; Q2 did not describe a terminated deal.

  • Q3 backlog commentary pointed to growth from June to September, while Q2 highlighted converting backlog into shipments and ended with a lower backlog level.

  • Analyst Q3 questions concentrated on margin trajectory and European growth mechanics, whereas Q2 included broader questions on order book breadth and “elephant” deals.

Risks and Concerns

  • "The opening of Beam Middle East hasn't turned out to be ideally timed as it's coincided with the war in the Gulf, which has had a negative impact on investment in the area." (CEO Wheatley) "It's just being postponed while this war goes on." (CEO Wheatley)

  • CEO Wheatley described Ukraine as an opportunity but operating in a war zone, stating "in the event that there is an attack, I may have to leave this call abruptly," while also emphasizing urgency-driven demand for BeamHeat.

  • CEO Wheatley flagged capital-markets perception risk tied to liquidity, saying the company has "maintain[ed] relatively low cash balances" and is "considering steps to remove the perception" of being "close to running out of cash."

Final Takeaway

Beam Global management framed Q3 around improved gross margin performance, rising backlog, and a business mix increasingly driven by commercial and international demand, while positioning Yuma manufacturing changes as a cost lever. CEO Wheatley highlighted BeamHeat as a new product with near-term demand signals tied to blackout conditions and described the decision to walk away from the ScoutDI acquisition amid share-price volatility, while also laying out a revenue-based pathway to positive cash flow anchored by quarterly volume growth.

data.title: Everpure anticipates Q4 revenue of $1.505B to $1.515B as it raises FY27 revenue outlook to $5.200B to $5.210B
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Everpure, Inc. (P) Q3 fiscal 2027

Management View

  • "Q3 was another strong quarter for Everpure" and "We exceeded our guidance range on both the top and bottom lines," said (Chairman & CEO Charles Giancarlo), citing "Revenue growth of 51% year-on-year" and "Operating profit surged 76% year-on-year to $345 million, resulting in a record 24% operating margin."

  • (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) emphasized that "the vast majority of our dollar revenue growth in Q3 came from our core business" while "revenue percentage growth in new business grew faster than the company average," and added, "We are beginning to see a significant upturn in the number of enterprises now adding GPU environments on-prem."

  • On product and platform updates, (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) said "FlashBlade//S is proving to be the go-to workhorse in enterprise AI factory build-outs" and noted a new feature: "we further improved FlashBlade AI system performance by delivering PureKVA... to deliver up to 20x faster time to first token for large language models."

  • On subscriptions and competitive displacements, (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) said "TCV for Evergreen//One continues its strong trajectory with 9 straight quarters of double-digit growth, reaching 57% year-over-year in Q3" and described a large insurance customer "replacing a legacy competitor" to standardize on Evergreen//One.

  • On new growth vectors, (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) said "Hyperscale solutions, scale AI and modern data software delivered a strong quarter" and added "Hyperscale solutions led this growth with sales increasing substantially during the quarter and continued expansion expected next quarter and into next year."

  • (Chief Financial Officer Tarek Robbiati) said "Revenue increased 51% year-over-year, while operating profit grew 76%" and "Our operating margin reached 23.6%, the highest in company history," adding that results reflected "broad-based momentum across our business" and "meaningful progress across all 3 new revenue opportunities."

Outlook

  • Q4 revenue guidance of $1.505B to $1.515B vs. $1.48645294B (analysts’ estimate); FY27 revenue guidance of $5.200B to $5.210B was provided, but no analysts’ FY27 revenue estimate was included in the provided estimates data.

  • (CFO Robbiati) said, "we are once again raising our full year revenue growth guidance" and guided Q4 operating profit to "$350 million to $360 million" and FY27 operating profit to "$1.08 billion to $1.09 billion."

  • Management reiterated a prior longer-range view rather than issuing a new guide: (CFO Robbiati) said, "We are also reiterating our fiscal year '28 preliminary outlook as presented at our Financial Analyst Day in September." In Q&A, (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) added, "we're not guiding on a fiscal '28" and "It wasn't a guide. It was flavor."

Financial Results

  • (CFO Robbiati) reported Q3 product revenue "increased 77% year-over-year to $948 million" and subscription services revenue "increased 19% year-over-year to $512 million."

  • (CFO Robbiati) said ARR "grew 20% year-over-year to more than $2.2 billion" and RPO "increased 44% year-over-year to more than $4.1 billion," while cautioning that "as we begin to lap those particularly strong quarters, we expect year-over-year comparisons to become more challenging."

  • On Storage-as-a-Service, (CFO Robbiati) said TCV sales "grew 57% year-over-year to $188 million" and added TCV was "accelerating towards an annualized run rate exceeding $1 billion in fiscal year '27."

  • (CFO Robbiati) reported Q3 total gross margin of "69.2%" with product gross margin of "67.3%" and subscription services gross margin of "72.6%," attributing subscription margin pressure "primarily" to "higher bonus accruals and costs of spares."

  • (CFO Robbiati) reported cash and investments of "over $1.1 billion," cash flow from operations of "$443 million," capital expenditures of "$178 million," and free cash flow of "$265 million" ("18.1%" free cash flow margin). He also said Everpure repurchased "542,000 shares" for "approximately $67 million" and had "about $109 million remaining" under the authorization.

Q&A

  • Amit Daryanani, Evercore ISI: asked what changed in buying behavior and durability; (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) responded, "we're picking up market share" and cited "increases in what we would call franchise deals" plus a shift where customers are "focusing on those things that are of critical importance" and "a shift towards higher performance, higher scale, lower latency workloads."

  • Howard Ma, Guggenheim: asked about pricing and Q4 price cuts; (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) said list price changes "will flow directly to the Street" and described reductions "on average" enabled by value engineering while "operating at the lower end of our 65% to 70% range."

  • Wamsi Mohan, BofA: pressed on hyperscale resilience and “hotter data”; (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) said Everpure is insulated because it has "such a small share going into the hyperscale market" and "a superior solution," adding "we're seeing the buying patterns trend towards higher performance products" and "hotter workloads generally means higher performance systems, which means higher ASPs."

  • Hadi Orabi (for TD Cowen): questioned why FY28 view unchanged after FY27 raise; (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) said, "we're not guiding on next year's" and "no one should take anything away from the fact that we did not raise a non-guide for FY '28."

  • Simon Leopold, Raymond James: asked about royalty trajectory and second hyperscaler timing; (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) said revenue was "exactly what we expected" and added, "we do expect to ship next year, probably towards -- beginning towards the middle of the year."

  • Joseph Cardoso, JPMorgan: asked about product gross margin drivers and Q4 implications; (CFO Robbiati) said uplift was "due to the contribution of new revenue, including hyperscalers" but Everpure "won't disclose the quantum," and added, "you can expect moving forward that we stick to our long-term guidance range of 65% to 70%" excluding new revenue.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was positive, with repeated praise such as "Congrats on some really impressive numbers" (Amit Daryanani, Evercore ISI) and "Outstanding performance" (Howard Ma, Guggenheim), while questions centered on pricing, hyperscale timing, and the FY27/FY28 framing.

  • Management tone was confident in prepared remarks and largely steady in Q&A, emphasizing share gains and control levers: "we view this as a market share game" (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) and "once again raising our full year revenue growth guidance" (CFO Robbiati).

  • Versus the prior quarter, Q3 retained an upbeat posture but included more explicit debate over forward visibility, with management repeatedly clarifying FY28 as "not... a guide" (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo), reflecting heightened sensitivity to how investors interpret longer-range commentary.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 featured a sharper growth profile, with "Revenue growth of 51% year-on-year" (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) versus Q2’s "Revenue growth of 38% year-over-year" (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo in Q2), alongside Q3’s record operating margin framing ("23.6%... highest in company history," CFO Robbiati).

  • Pricing posture shifted from Q2’s emphasis on operating at decade-high pricing levels to Q3’s announced reductions: "Beginning in Q4, we reduced pricing on average across most of our product models" (CFO Robbiati).

  • Hyperscale narrative progressed from Q2’s second top-5 hyperscaler agreement and expectations for FY28 ramp to Q3 focus on royalties being included in product revenue and near-term pacing: "product revenue now includes royalties generated from our hyperscale solutions business" (CFO Robbiati) and the second hyperscaler contribution this year being "de minimis" (CFO Robbiati in Q&A).

  • Analyst focus evolved from Q2’s supply-tightness and price elasticity discussion toward Q3 scrutiny of price cuts, hyperscale royalty cadence, and whether higher FY27 implied pull-forward into FY28.

Risks and Concerns

  • (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) said "component costs continue to increase through Q3" and added "the macro backdrop continues to change rapidly," while also stating, "We expect component costs to stabilize towards the end of the year and to remain high going into next year."

  • Management flagged pricing volatility and demand elasticity dynamics: (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) said customers are dealing with prices "over 100% higher" in parts of the industry, and later noted, "If prices suddenly drop, we're going to have a different several quarters."

  • On subscription profitability pressures, (CFO Robbiati) attributed subscription services margin decline "primarily" to "higher bonus accruals and costs of spares" and said the company would "continue to closely monitor component costs and market conditions."

Final Takeaway

Everpure management described Q3 as a quarter where core demand and emerging growth vectors both contributed to results, with (Chairman & CEO Giancarlo) highlighting GPU-adjacent enterprise momentum and new product capabilities, and (CFO Robbiati) raising FY27 revenue and operating profit guidance while positioning Q4 price reductions as enabled by value engineering. In Q&A, management repeatedly framed the hyperscale opportunity around share gains and reiterated that FY28 commentary remained a preliminary view rather than formal guidance, while analysts focused on the implications of price cuts, hyperscale royalties and timing, and the relationship between the FY27 raise and next-year expectations.

data.title: Cintas Chairman met with Trump to save the $5.5B UniFirst deal - Semafor
data.description:
Cintas (CTAS) Chairman Scott Farmer met with President Donald Trump recently to try to salvage its $5.5 billion purchase of rival UniFirst (UNF), as the Federal Trade Commission may sue to block the combination.

Farmer met with Trump to try to have him intervene as FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson appears inclined to challenge the deal, according to a Semafor report on Wednesday, which cited an administration official and people familiar with the matter. Cintas (CTAS) and the family that controls the uniform company have donated to the president's 2016 inauguration and helped him raise hundreds of thousands of dollars.

The president has signaled that he will defer to Ferguson's judgment, one person familiar told Semafor.

Cintas (CTAS) has engaged legal counsel and expects the FTC to file a lawsuit, according to the report. Cintas has indicated to some investors that it may seek a divestiture package to try to thwart a lawsuit, though internally the company doesn't appear to want to divest.

Cintas declined to comment to Semafor.  Spokespeople for the FTC and White House didn't immediately respond with a comment.

The Semafor story comes after a report earlier Wednesday that companies were cautiously optimistic that the FTC would clear the combination unconditionally and are planning for integration. The FTC hasn't come to a decision, and the two companies are working on other methods for clearance, according to traders, who cited a Capitol Forum report. UniFirst executives met Tuesday to discuss ways to close the deal.   

The Unifirst/Cintas deal spread narrowed to $85 on Wednesday from $100 on Tuesday following the Capitol Forum report. Cintas (CTAS) agreed to acquire smaller rival UniFirst (UNF) for $310 per share in cash and stock in March, representing an enterprise value of about $5.5B.

The latest reports come after Semafor on Friday reported that the FTC will soon have a “last rites” meeting with the parties. These meetings between the antitrust regulator and the parties are typically a precursor to a formal lawsuit.

Last month, UniFirst (UNF) and Cintas (CTAS) disclosed that they certified to the FTC that each had substantially complied with the regulator's second request. Cintas and UniFirst entered into a timing agreement with the FTC pursuant to which they would not consummate the deal before Dec. 11.

data.title: Uti expects $925M-$945M fiscal 2027 revenue while targeting 34,000-35,500 starts
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Universal Technical Institute (UTI) Q4 fiscal 2026

Management View

  • "We finished fiscal 2026 with our North Star strategy on track" and "we remain confident that we will exceed $1.2 billion in revenue and approach $220 million in adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2029" (CEO Jerome Grant).
  • "Revenue grew 7% year-over-year to $897 million" and "starts came in below where we wanted them to be" even as "in the quarter, we still grew by 3% year-over-year" (CEO Grant).
  • "We're confident that the changes and enhancements we have implemented have fixed the high school admissions issue" and "our goal is to add up to 1,000 seats to existing programs by the end of fiscal 2027" (CEO Grant).
  • "We're also taking modest pricing actions on our skilled trade programs" and "today, we're introducing the next generation of UTI campuses" called "Skilled Trades Max" (CEO Grant).
  • "Fourth quarter revenue on a consolidated basis increased 6% to $235.9 million" and "consolidated net income for the fourth quarter was $18.0 million or $0.32 per diluted share" (Executive VP & CFO Bruce Schuman).
  • "In August, we signed a new $200 million revolving credit facility, up from $125 million" and "we have more than sufficient resources to fund the remainder of North Star Phase 2 without the need for any new financing" (CFO Schuman).

Outlook

  • "For fiscal 2027, we expect new student starts of 34,000 to 35,500" and "we expect revenue of $925 million to $945 million this year" (CFO Schuman).
  • "The softer Q4 2026 cohort creates a lower entering student population for fiscal 2027 and therefore, moderates near-term revenue growth" and "this is the dynamic in our student base specific to fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027" (CFO Schuman).
  • "The revenue outlook this year, combined with planned growth investments as well as the onetime integration and restructuring costs" is expected to result in "a net income outlook of $0 to $5 million for the year" and "diluted earnings per share of $0.00 to $0.09" (CFO Schuman).
  • "Baseline adjusted EBITDA is expected to be $135 million to $141 million" and "we expect reported adjusted EBITDA to be between $100 million and $106 million" (CFO Schuman).
  • "We expect to execute on $160 million to $170 million of capital expenditures in fiscal 2027" (CFO Schuman).

Financial Results

  • "Fourth quarter revenue on a consolidated basis increased 6% to $235.9 million" with "Concorde" at "$82.2 million" and "the UTI division" at "$153.6 million" (CFO Schuman).
  • "For the full year, consolidated revenue grew 7.4% to $897 million" with "Concorde" at "$319.8 million" and "the UTI division" at "$577.2 million" (CFO Schuman).
  • "Consolidated net income for the fourth quarter was $18.0 million" and "$33.6 million" for the full year (CFO Schuman).
  • "Baseline adjusted EBITDA was $49.5 million for the fourth quarter and $136.6 million for the full year" while "our SEC reported adjusted EBITDA was $42.5 million for the fourth quarter and $102 million for the full year" (CFO Schuman).
  • "For the year, capital expenditures were $112.9 million" and "total available liquidity at the end of the year was $321 million" (CFO Schuman).

Q&A

  • Steven Frankel, Rosenblatt: Asked how starts growth can be modest if skilled trades demand is seat-constrained and whether there is deceleration in auto/diesel; CEO Grant: "the softness we saw in the fourth quarter was highly concentrated to auto diesel" and "that's why we've enhanced our growth agenda to focus also on creating 1,000 new seats of capacity".
  • Steven Frankel, Rosenblatt: Asked about pulling missed high school students into the December quarter; CEO Grant: "we're not reporting on the first quarter right now" and "we'll report on that when we do the first quarter".
  • Steven Frankel, Rosenblatt: Asked about replicating the Heartland co-branded model to reduce capital intensity; CEO Grant: "we're in deep conversations with them and other parties" including "things like HVAC and aviation".
  • Eric Martinuzzi, Lake Street: Asked whether mix shift toward shorter skilled trades pressures margins and FY29 EBITDA margin; CEO Grant: "as we scale up these businesses and create capacity on it, that margin gap will shrink" and "our confidence hasn't wavered" on "approaching $220 million in EBITDA".
  • Griffin Boss, B. Riley: Asked why midpoint revenue growth lags starts growth in FY27 guidance; CFO Schuman: "that is really the only disconnect" and "it is that carry-in issue from the Q4".
  • Jasper Bibb, Truist: Pressed on higher FY27 CapEx and whether builds are more capital intensive; CFO Schuman: "fundamentally, it's really a timing issue" and "the vast majority is growth" ("50%" new campuses, "over 15%" replications/new programs, and "a full 10%" skilled trades expansions).
  • Jasper Bibb, Truist: Asked about buybacks vs. growth spend; CEO Grant: "we're staying the course" and "'26 and '27 were going to be significant investment years to load the machine for '28 and '29".
  • Mike Grondahl, Northland: Asked about auto/diesel utilization and repurposing space; CEO Grant: "we're 40% to 50% capacity in our auto diesel" and "we're thinking very deeply about how we reimagine how auto diesel is being taught".

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly negative to pressing, with repeated probing on the Q4 high school/auto-diesel shortfall, the starts-to-revenue bridge, and elevated CapEx (e.g., "I'm just trying to square in my mind" and "I'm just kind of struggling to bridge" from Steven Frankel and Jasper Bibb).
  • Management: slightly positive and corrective in tone, emphasizing fixes and long-term targets (e.g., "we believe we've corrected course" and "our confidence hasn't wavered" from CEO Grant; "that is really the only disconnect" from CFO Schuman).
  • Versus last quarter: management messaging shifted from identifying execution issues to asserting remediation progress (Q4: "fixed the high school admissions issue"; Q3: "we have unfortunately seen some near-term softness" and "we are proactively taking steps").

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • High school channel: Q3 flagged execution shortfalls ("we simply did not get to all the prospective students") while Q4 asserted remediation ("our UTI high school admissions team is now fully staffed" and "high school presentations and enrollments for 2027 fall term are already significantly up").
  • Capacity constraints: Q4 introduced a quantified near-term capacity target ("add up to 1,000 seats") and operational tactics ("we're offering welding sections after midnight"), expanding beyond Q3’s focus on improving execution and ongoing capacity work.
  • Investment cadence: Q3 guided FY26 revenue "$893 million to $900 million" and reported adjusted EBITDA "$100 million to $103 million"; Q4 finalized FY26 at "$897 million" and "$102 million" and set FY27 CapEx at "$160 million to $170 million".
  • Strategy detail: Q4 added the "Skilled Trades Max" campus model and explicitly laid out "4 more" campuses in FY27 and plans to open "4 more" in each of FY28 and FY29.

Risks and Concerns

  • "Personnel challenges in our high school admissions channel" and "capacity constraints" were cited as factors that "put a damper on our Q4 2026 performance" (CEO Grant).
  • "The softer Q4 2026 cohort creates a lower entering student population for fiscal 2027" (CFO Schuman).
  • "On the marketing side, the shift towards zero-click search and AI-driven discovery requires continued investment" (CEO Grant).
  • "Onetime integration and restructuring costs to unify and simplify the company and move to a single operating structure" were included in FY27 outlook (CFO Schuman).

Final Takeaway

Management framed fiscal 2026 as a growth-and-investment year that still produced $897 million in revenue and set up an FY27 plan centered on rebuilding high school admissions execution, adding up to 1,000 incremental skilled-trades seats by the end of FY27, and funding a heavier build cycle. The company’s FY27 outlook called for 34,000 to 35,500 starts and $925 million to $945 million revenue, while reiterating longer-term North Star targets to exceed $1.2 billion in revenue and approach $220 million in adjusted EBITDA by fiscal 2029.

data.title: U.S. oil price slides as data shows larger-than-expected increases in crude, gasoline stocks
data.description:
Crude oil futures fell Wednesday as the market continued to focus more on strong supply than on the conflict in the Middle East.

Oil was part of a broad retreat across commodities as the dollar strengthened to a fresh 19-month high, creating a headwind for raw materials priced in the currency.

The Brent crude benchmark has retreated by more than 20% so far this month, as supplies from the Middle East recovered and President Trump held off on renewed large-scale strikes against Iran, although low-level fighting has flared up across the region recently.

While recovering Middle East supply keeps crude under pressure, continued attacks on vessels around the Strait of Hormuz and renewed strikes on Persian Gulf infrastructure "highlight the fragility of this recovery," Sparta Commodities oil analyst Abhishek Kumar said in a note.

Russian refining is still disrupted by Ukrainian attacks, with crude exports rising as refinery outages limit domestic processing, developments that "continue to support a geopolitical premium in European diesel despite the broader weakness in crude," Kumar added.

The decline in U.S. crude futures was exacerbated by the U.S. Energy Information Administration's weekly report showing larger-than-expected increases in crude oil and gasoline inventories, adding to expectations of a supply surplus.

U.S. commercial crude oil stocks excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve rose by 3.4M barrels to 417.8M in the week ended November 13 and were 3% below the five-year average for the time of year, according to the EIA.

U.S. gasoline inventories increased by 5.2M barrels to 215.9M barrels and were 3% above the five-year average for the time of year, and distillate fuel stocks rose by 1.6M barrels to 104.9M barrels and were 7% below the five-year average for the time of year, the EIA said.

The stock builds added to selling pressure, Gelber & Associates analysts said, adding, "Attacks involving Iran and commercial shipping ​still threaten deliveries through the Strait of Hormuz, but those risks have provided limited support against the growing expectation of a global surplus."

On Wednesday, front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for December delivery fell 3.2% to $83.26/bbl, its lowest settlement value since August 26, and front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for January delivery slipped 1.3% to $91.95/bbl, its lowest close since November 10.

Additionally, front-month Nymex December natural gas (NG1:COM) rose 5.1% to $3.372/MMBtu, its best settlement value since February 6, as cooler weather forecasts improved the near-term demand outlook.

ETFs: (USO), (BNO), (UCO), (SCO), (USL), (DBO), (DRIP), (GUSH), (USOI), (UNG), (BOIL), (KOLD), (UNL), (FCG), (XLE), (XOP)

data.title: Venture Global CEO sees final investment decisions on two key projects in next year's H1
data.description:
Venture Global's (VG) growth plans have progressed well, and the company intends to make final investment decisions for the expansion of its CP2 and Plaquemines projects in next year's H1, and some equipment orders have already been placed, CEO Michael Sabel told The Wall Street Journal in an interview Wednesday.

Venture Global (VG) is advancing the two expansion projects to push its liquefied natural gas production capacity past 100M metric tons/year before the end of 2030.

The expansion at CP2 is expected to provide an additional 10M tons/year of LNG, and the Plaquemines expansion should increase production by 7M-8M tons/year.

LNG suppliers and analysts are split between those that forecast an impending supply glut once energy markets stabilize and those that expect demand will continue to rise, but Sabel told WSJ that the company does not believe there is a supply glut.

Instead, Venture Global (VG) expects a small LNG shortage heading into the early 2030s with large supply projects likely to run behind schedule, Sabel said.

The outlook is also clouded by questions over when lost volumes from Qatar will return to the market, as damage to the country's facilities from the Middle East conflict has cut the country’s export capacity by ~17%.

data.title: Wheat leads U.S. grain futures lower, falling to lowest since January
data.description:
CBOT December wheat futures fell $0.25 to $5.70 per bushel on Wednesday, the contract's lowest level since January, leading the market lower as part of a broad selloff in commodities.

The dollar rallied to a 19-month high on rising expectations for an interest rate hike next month, which could further weigh on demand by making U.S. grains less competitive in the global market.

Overall commodity sentiment is in a state of deflation, Gary Sandlund of Futures International said in a note, pointing to sharp declines in oil and gold, "just to name a few," while geopolitical tensions seem to be the "new normal" and markets have adapted to it.

U.S. wheat prices had gained in the previous session after a Ukrainian attack destroyed parts of the Crimea bridge, threatening further disruption to Russian wheat exports.

"Shipments have already been effectively nonexistent relative to pre-war norms, but this damage could mean a substantial delay to resumed commodity flow even if an agreement was somehow reached," Mike Castle of StoneX wrote.

The market also continues to wonder whether China will agree to buy U.S. corn when Presidents Trump and Xi meet this week, as analysts say export demand remains a central focus for the corn market following its sluggish start to the marketing year.

CBOT wheat (W_1:COM) for December delivery plunged 4.2% to $5.70 per bushel, corn (C_1:COM) for December delivery dropped 2.5% to $4.35 1/2 per bushel, and January soybean (S_1:COM) slipped 0.7% to 12.16 3/4 per bushel.
